tracks.narration: Two equations, two unknowns — what does row reduction do to the picture?
Here is a system. Two lines on the plane. They cross at one point — that crossing is the unique solution.
Swap the rows so the small leading coefficient is on top. The lines didn't move — we only renamed which equation we call row one.
Now replace row two with row two minus two times row one. The second line tilts and shifts — but watch the intersection. It does not move.
One more step — divide and back-substitute. The lines become axis-aligned. The matrix is upper triangular. The solution is just read off.
Row operations slide and tilt the lines, but they cannot move the answer. Elimination is a change of view, not a change of truth.
